name: Vite
summary: A frontend development and build system that maintains environment-specific module graphs, transforms modules on demand through a plugin container, serves native ESM with HMR, pre-bundles dependencies, and produces optimized build outputs.
scope: on-demand module graph and transform server

features.name: On-demand module graph server
features.description: The fixed server creates development environments with module graphs whose nodes track URLs, resolved files, importers, imported modules, transform results, and invalidation state. Requests resolve and transform modules on demand instead of requiring a complete application bundle before serving the first page.
benefits: Supports fast startup and per-module transformation
Makes importer relationships and invalidation targets explicit
costs: Graph state and transform caches can become stale or fragmented
Unbundled development exposes browser request and compatibility constraints

features.name: Plugin and environment pipeline
features.description: Vite constructs a plugin container and invokes ordered plugin hooks for resolution, loading, transformation, hot updates, and build integration. The environment-aware server and build APIs provide shared extension points while allowing client, SSR, and other environments to carry distinct module state.
benefits: Extends resolution and transformation without hard-coding every framework
Allows environment-specific behavior behind a common plugin contract
costs: Hook ordering and environment differences can produce non-obvious interactions
Plugin authors must preserve graph and cache invariants

features.name: Dependency pre-bundling
features.description: Vite documents dependency pre-bundling as a development optimization that converts dependencies to a browser-friendly form and reduces repeated nested dependency requests. The fixed source exposes optimizer state alongside the development server pipeline.
benefits: Reduces dependency request overhead during development
Normalizes packages that are awkward to consume as native browser ESM
costs: Optimizer invalidation and package discovery add a separate cache lifecycle
Pre-bundled output can differ from application source transformation behavior

features.name: Production build and output pipeline
features.description: The Vite build API resolves build configuration and invokes the production bundling pipeline, while official documentation distinguishes development serving from optimized production output. The build emits chunks and assets according to configured targets and output options.
benefits: Separates low-latency development serving from optimized deployment artifacts
Supports framework and asset transforms through the same configuration surface
costs: Two execution modes require parity testing for transforms and environment behavior
Output chunking and asset policy affect deployment performance and correctness

mathematical_views.question: How do module imports, transformed results, and invalidation states evolve independently across Vite environments?
assumptions: Each environment has a graph whose nodes represent resolved modules and transform state
Importer edges are sufficient to model HMR propagation at this abstraction level
Filesystem watching, browser scheduling, and bundler internals are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which ordered plugin hooks map a request or build module from unresolved input to transformed output?
assumptions: Hook order is modeled as a transition sequence over resolve, load, transform, and update operations
Plugin return values are treated as the boundary state passed to later hooks
The view does not prove that arbitrary plugins compose successfully

mathematical_views.question: Which module and asset properties are preserved when a project moves from on-demand development transforms to production bundling?
assumptions: Development and production are separate execution paths with shared configuration and plugin concepts
Preservation means intended module semantics, not identical request graphs or filenames
Minification, target support, and deployment behavior require separate validation

benefits: Fast feedback through per-module serving and invalidation
costs: Browser request volume and graph cache coherence become operational concerns
Hook ordering and cross-environment compatibility increase integration surface

benefits: Fewer development requests and normalized dependencies
costs: Discovery and optimizer caches require invalidation policy

benefits: Optimized deployable artifacts distinct from dev serving
costs: Maintaining dev/build parity adds pipeline complexity
